# 09 Lay out namespace frames and notes

## Outcome

`layoutClassDiagram` maps namespaces onto the shared core's cluster support and places notes:
a namespace becomes a cluster whose frame encloses its member classes, and a note becomes a
sized box — attached notes joined to their class, free notes placed without a connector.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A namespace with two member classes returns a frame box enclosing both class boxes with
  padding, plus a position for its label.
- [ ] A class in no namespace is laid out normally and is not enclosed by any frame.
- [ ] An attached note returns a box sized to its text plus a connector path from the box to its
  target class's box.
- [ ] A free note returns a box and no connector.
- [ ] Notes do not overlap class boxes — a note's box intersects no class box in the returned
  geometry.
- [ ] `width`/`height` grow to contain namespace frames and note boxes.
- [ ] `PositionedClass.name` includes the class's generic parameter. Round 2 set it to `cls.id`,
  dropping `cls.generic` — which contradicts the field's own contract in `contracts.ts` ("the
  class-name text as drawn, **including any generic parameter**") and spec.md's criterion that
  generics render as part of the class name. The box must also be measured from the composed
  name, not the bare id, or a generic name overflows its frame. Found in round 2's review; ticket
  10 asserts the rendering, so this must land first or that assertion cannot pass.
- [ ] Everything from ticket 04 still holds — its tests pass unmodified.

## Test seam

`layoutClassDiagram(model, options): PositionedClassDiagram` — unit level, fake measurer,
extending ticket 04's test file.
